segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 我叫 Catherine。

segments.en: And today we have a very advanced lesson for you all about medicine.
segments.zh: 今天，我们为大家提供了一个非常先进的课程关于医学。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to take a look at what is very widely known as Chinese traditional medicine.
segments.zh: 今天我们来看看什么是广为人知的中药。

segments.en: So a very interesting topic in general.
segments.zh: 所以一般来说是一个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And for people who use this, they might call it TCM, traditional Chinese medicine.
segments.zh: 对于使用它的人来说，他们可能会称之为 TCM，也就是传统中医。

segments.en: So remember that there's that acronym as well.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，还有那个首字母缩略词。

segments.en: But let's take a listen to today's dialogue and when we come back, we'll be discussing some of the important words and phrases in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 但是让我们听听今天的对话，当我们回来时，我们将讨论对话中的一些重要单词和短语。

segments.en: What's wrong?
segments.zh: 怎么了？

segments.en: I have a headache.
segments.zh: 我头疼。

segments.en: These past few days I've been living off painkillers.
segments.zh: 这几天我全靠止痛药撑着。

segments.en: Man, I feel like my head is going to explode.
segments.zh: 哎呀，头疼得快炸了。

segments.en: You should get acupuncture treatment.
segments.zh: 你应该去做针灸。

segments.en: My mom was always having headache issues and it was acupuncture that cured her.
segments.zh: 我妈以前经常头疼，后来是针灸治好的。

segments.en: The results are too slow.
segments.zh: 那见效太慢了。

segments.en: On top of that, just the thought of smoking needles poking into my flesh frightens me.
segments.zh: 而且光想到那些冒着烟的针扎进肉里，我就害怕。

segments.en: They don't just randomly stick you.
segments.zh: 针可不是随便乱扎的。

segments.en: They find your pressure points.
segments.zh: 医生会找准穴位。

segments.en: The heat allows the body to immediately respond to the treatment, restoring the body's qi.
segments.zh: 热力能让身体迅速对治疗作出反应，恢复体内的“气”。

segments.en: But I get scared the moment I see a needle.
segments.zh: 可我一见到针就害怕。

segments.en: How could I stand having needles in my body for hours on end?
segments.zh: 让我身上扎着针，一扎就是几个小时，我怎么受得了？

segments.en: The needles are very thin.
segments.zh: 针其实很细。

segments.en: And as long as the doctor's technique is good and the patient himself is relaxed, it won't hurt.
segments.zh: 只要医生手法好、病人放松，就不会疼。

segments.en: On the contrary, it will actually alleviate pain.
segments.zh: 相反，还能缓解疼痛。

segments.en: Now there are high-tech needles that are micro-thin.
segments.zh: 现在还有极细的高科技针。

segments.en: They don't hurt at all.
segments.zh: 扎起来一点也不疼。

segments.en: However, if you are really scared of acupuncture, scraping or cupping are also options.
segments.zh: 如果你实在怕针灸，也可以试试刮痧或拔罐。

segments.en: Scraping is too terrifying.
segments.zh: 刮痧更吓人。

segments.en: When they finish scraping, your body is all red as if you were just tortured.
segments.zh: 刮完浑身通红，像刚受过刑一样。

segments.en: Cupping is the same.
segments.zh: 拔罐也一样。

segments.en: Your body ends up with red circles all over it.
segments.zh: 身上会留下一圈圈红印。

segments.en: It looks like someone beat you up.
segments.zh: 看着像被人揍了一顿。

segments.en: This only signifies that the toxins have left the body.
segments.zh: 那只是说明体内的毒素排出来了。

segments.en: Actually, there's only discomfort during the treatment process.
segments.zh: 其实只有治疗过程中会有些不舒服。

segments.en: Once it's over, you'll feel very comfortable.
segments.zh: 做完以后就舒服了。

segments.en: Chinese medicine is strange.
segments.zh: 中医很奇怪。

segments.en: The patients are already ill and then the doctor makes them suffer more.
segments.zh: 病人本来就不舒服，医生还让他们受更多罪。

segments.en: This is the only way to get at the problem.
segments.zh: 只有这样才能治到根上。

segments.en: Anyway, if you want to relieve the pain, you are just going to have to be tough and do it.
segments.zh: 总之，要想止疼，你就得硬着头皮试一试。

segments.en: Forget it.
segments.zh: 算了。

segments.en: I don't want to inflict any more pain on myself.
segments.zh: 我可不想再让自己受罪了。

segments.en: In a little while, I'll go and buy some more painkillers and take a nap.
segments.zh: 我过会儿再去买些止痛药，然后睡一觉。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now obviously we are talking about what is commonly known as alternative medicine because we know that traditional medicine nowadays is doctors, you have antibiotics, that sort of thing.
segments.zh: 所以现在显然我们在谈论通常被称为替代医学的东西，因为我们知道现在的传统医学是医生，你有抗生素之类的东西。

segments.en: And here you're actually using these techniques and these different ways of curing someone.
segments.zh: 在这里，您实际上正在使用这些技术和这些不同的治愈方法。

segments.en: So the first thing that comes to mind here is acupuncture.
segments.zh: 所以这里首先想到的是针灸。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So acupuncture is usually considered a part of Chinese medicine and it's a kind of medicine that uses needles in different parts of the body.
segments.zh: 所以针灸通常被认为是中医的一部分，它是一种在身体不同部位使用针头的疗法。

segments.en: So it might look really scary because you see people lying on their stomachs with needles coming out of their backs.
segments.zh: 所以它可能看起来真的很可怕，因为你看到人们趴着，针从背上伸出来。

segments.en: And the places where they put the needles in, they're called pressure points, right?
segments.zh: 还有他们把针扎进去的地方，它们被称为穴位，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And pressure points are things that we talk about with massages as well.
segments.zh: 我们谈按摩时也会提到穴位。

segments.en: So a good masseuse, a person who does a massage, will also look for these pressure points, which are key points on the body.
segments.zh: 所以好的按摩师，也就是做按摩的人，也会寻找这些穴位，它们是身体上的关键点。

segments.en: And in acupuncture, they'll put these needles into those points as well because each point relates to a different part of the body, like the liver or the kidneys.
segments.zh: 在针灸中，他们也会将这些针头放在这些点上，因为每个点都与身体的不同部位有关，例如肝脏或肾脏。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's actually very interesting, the fact that by sticking a needle in one of these pressure points, they are curing or alleviating the pain of maybe, like you say, your kidney or your liver or something like this.
segments.zh: 所以这其实很有意思：通过在其中某个穴位上扎针，他们就能治愈或减轻——就像你说的——你的肾脏、肝脏之类部位的疼痛。

segments.en: This is a really great word though, Marco, the word that you just used, to alleviate pain.
segments.zh: 不过，这是一个非常棒的词，Marco，你刚刚使用的这个词来减轻痛苦。

segments.en: Now to alleviate pain means to make the pain go away.
segments.zh: 现在减轻疼痛意味着让疼痛消失。

segments.en: So we heard the opposite of that as well, also at the very end of today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我们也听到了意思相反的词，就在今天对话的最后也听到了。

segments.en: So the opposite of alleviate would be to inflict pain.
segments.zh: 所以减轻的反面是造成痛苦。

segments.en: This is to do pain to yourself or to someone else.
segments.zh: 这是对自己或别人施加痛苦。

segments.en: To cause pain.
segments.zh: 引起疼痛。

segments.en: To cause pain.
segments.zh: 引起疼痛。

segments.en: So to alleviate is to take it away and to inflict is to cause.
segments.zh: 所以 alleviate 就是消除疼痛，而 inflict 就是造成疼痛。

segments.en: So now acupuncture is very popular.
segments.zh: 所以现在针灸很受欢迎。

segments.en: Sticking needles in people's pressure points, it does seem like it would hurt, but there are other ones that maybe are not as widely known.
segments.zh: 在人们的穴位上扎针，看起来确实会疼，但还有其他一些可能不那么广为人知的疗法。

segments.en: The next one that we're going to talk about is scraping.
segments.zh: 我们要讨论的下一个是刮痧。

segments.en: Scraping.
segments.zh: 刮痧。

segments.en: So to scrape is a verb and you can scrape the bottom of your plate with your spoon or you can scrape on, you know, sometimes cats like to scrape on the furniture.
segments.zh: 所以刮是一个动词，你可以用勺子刮掉盘子的底部，或者你可以刮，你知道，有时猫喜欢在家具上刮擦。

segments.en: They use their claws and make that sound.
segments.zh: 它们用爪子发出那种声音。

segments.en: But in this case, scraping is a little bit more maybe painful sounding.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，刮擦可能听起来有点痛苦。

segments.en: What do they do in scraping?
segments.zh: 他们在刮擦时做什么？

segments.en: So basically it's the same thing.
segments.zh: 所以基本上是一样的。

segments.en: They use different tools and they scrape your body.
segments.zh: 他们使用不同的工具，会刮伤你的身体。

segments.en: They just, I don't know, basically what I understand from it is that they are extracting the illness by taking it out of your skin.
segments.zh: 他们只是，我不知道，基本上我从中的理解是他们通过从你的皮肤中取出疾病来提取疾病。

segments.en: So they use what looks like a small knife or like a flat kind of sharp blade.
segments.zh: 所以他们使用看起来像一把小刀或像扁平的锋利刀片的东西。

segments.en: And they actually kind of take off the top layer of your skin.
segments.zh: 他们实际上会刮掉你皮肤的表层。

segments.en: They scrape it away.
segments.zh: 他们把它刮掉。

segments.en: It's very, very painful from what I've heard.
segments.zh: 从我听到的情况来看，这是非常非常痛苦的。

segments.en: I've never done it myself, but as we see in the dialogue, it does look very, it looks like you've been hit or treated poorly at the prison or something because your skin is red and almost bleeding.
segments.zh: 我自己从来没有做过，但正如我们在对话中看到的那样，看起来确实很吓人——就像你在监狱里挨了打或受了虐待一样，因为你的皮肤发红，几乎要流血。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And another one that actually looks quite painful when you see someone after they've done it is called cupping.
segments.zh: 还有一种疗法，当你看到别人做完之后的样子时，看起来相当痛苦，叫做拔罐。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Now, this one you might have seen even in the last Karate Kid movie.
segments.zh: 现在，即使在上一部空手道儿童电影中，您也可能看到过这部。

segments.en: Basically it's a little round bulb or a little round glass cup and the doctor, the Chinese doctor will light a piece of cotton and will put the cup over it and the suction effect that by putting out the fire and it sucks up all the oxygen and everything causes the cup to suck onto your skin really, really tight.
segments.zh: 基本上，它是一个小圆球或小圆玻璃罐，中国医生会点燃一块棉花，然后把罐子扣在上面，火一熄灭就产生抽吸效果，把里面的氧气都吸掉，这一切会让罐子紧紧吸附在你的皮肤上。

segments.en: You put it on your skin so it creates a vacuum, right?
segments.zh: 你把它放在你的皮肤上，这样它就会产生真空，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: There's no air coming in.
segments.zh: 没有空气进来。

segments.en: And that way the cup that there's no air in has to pull out all those chemicals and those toxins and that oil from your skin and take it away.
segments.zh: 这样一来，没有空气的杯子就必须从你的皮肤上排出所有这些化学物质和那些毒素以及油脂并将其带走。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's actually pulling at your skin.
segments.zh: 所以它实际上是在拉你的皮肤。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And well, that's the thing with the vacuum effect is so great and pulling it out with such force that you're actually left with a big purple or red circle on your skin from I guess the blood clot type thing that is caused by it.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是真空效果是如此之大，并且以如此大的力量将其拉出，以至于您实际上在皮肤上留下了一个大的紫色或红色圆圈，我猜是它引起的血凝块类型的东西。

segments.en: So you will see a person's back maybe and they have bruises.
segments.zh: 所以你可能会看到一个人的背部，他们有瘀伤。

segments.en: Bruises.
segments.zh: 瘀伤。

segments.en: Yeah, like six, seven, ten bruises on their backs.
segments.zh: 是的，就像他们的背上有六、七、十个瘀伤。

segments.en: Although I am told that even though it's very painful and it looks even more painful, the effect is that it does help your circulation.
segments.zh: 虽然有人告诉我，尽管它非常痛苦并且看起来更痛苦，但效果是它确实有助于您的血液循环。

segments.en: It helps the blood in your body move around more freely.
segments.zh: 它可以帮助您体内的血液更自由地移动。

segments.en: Yeah, I've heard the same thing.
segments.zh: 是的，我也听说过同样的事情。

segments.en: And even though that it looks painful and it may be painful while they're doing it, I've heard that after it's done, even though it looks like it should hurt, it looks like a bruise, it doesn't hurt like a bruise.
segments.zh: 尽管看起来很痛苦，而且在他们做的时候可能会很痛苦，但我听说完成后，即使看起来应该很痛，它看起来像瘀伤，它不会像瘀伤一样痛。

segments.en: So people don't actually say, oh, you know, don't touch my back.
segments.zh: 所以人们实际上并没有说，哦，你知道，不要碰我的背。

segments.en: It really hurts.
segments.zh: 真的很痛。

segments.en: It doesn't really seem that way.
segments.zh: 看起来不是真的那样。

segments.en: Well, and there's an interesting line in the dialogue that is related to this.
segments.zh: 好吧，对话中有一句与此相关的有趣台词。

segments.en: It's about scraping actually, but you can say it about cupping as well.
segments.zh: 这实际上是关于刮擦，但你也可以说关于拔罐。

segments.en: Your body is all red as if you were just tortured.
segments.zh: 你的身体是红色的，就像你只是被折磨了一样。

segments.en: Now as if you were tortured or we could say as if you were beaten up.
segments.zh: 现在好像你被折磨了，或者我们可以说你被殴打了。

segments.en: And in this case, was the person tortured?
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，这个人是否受到了折磨？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: It's basically a relation or making that relation that your skin is so, let's say bloody that it looks as if you were tortured.
segments.zh: 这基本上是在建立一种类比：你的皮肤红得，可以说，看起来就像你被折磨过一样。

segments.en: So it seems like somebody hit you with a whip or something.
segments.zh: 所以似乎有人用鞭子或其他东西打了你。

segments.en: It looks like you were tortured, but you weren't.
segments.zh: 看起来你被折磨了，但你没有。

segments.en: So as if is a way for us to make a comparison or an analogy.
segments.zh: 所以好像是我们进行比较或类比的一种方式。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think you can see it in maybe books, you know, so maybe you would describe a guy saying, oh, he was really angry as if he had rabies.
segments.zh: 我想你可以在书中看到它，你知道，所以也许你会描述一个人说，哦，他真的很生气，就好像他有狂犬病一样。

segments.en: Yeah, it's as if he had rabies like he doesn't, but he's acting like he does.
segments.zh: 是的，就好像他有狂犬病一样，但他的行为就像他一样。

segments.en: Or maybe you run into the kitchen and eat so much food as if you hadn't eaten in days.
segments.zh: 或者，也许你跑进厨房吃了这么多食物，就好像你几天没吃东西一样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you have obviously, but you're acting like someone who is starving.
segments.zh: 所以你显然并不是，但你表现得就像一个快饿死的人。

segments.en: So yeah, that is an interesting way to describe or to make a connection between two different things.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这是描述或在两个不同事物之间建立联系的有趣方式。

segments.en: And well, Chinese traditional medicine as well, a very interesting and historical form of treating illnesses.
segments.zh: 好吧，中医也是一种非常有趣、历史悠久的治病方式。

segments.en: Now I'm told that it does work, even though some people are very skeptical about it.
segments.zh: 现在我被告知它确实有效，尽管有些人对此持怀疑态度。

segments.en: And I don't think it's accepted in the international medical field.
segments.zh: 而且我不认为它在国际医学领域被接受。

segments.en: Well, I think that there's a Western medicine which has its benefits.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为西医有它的好处。

segments.en: You know, you have penicillin and all of these different antibiotics to help us combat different diseases and bacteria.
segments.zh: 你知道，你有青霉素和所有这些不同的抗生素来帮助我们对抗不同的疾病和细菌。

segments.en: But also traditional Chinese medicine kind of helps other things.
segments.zh: 而且中医对其它方面也有帮助。

segments.en: I think there is a spirituality, this idea that we have a chi, there are positive and negative forces in our bodies, and sometimes trauma or big events will make that chi kind of, well, it'll affect it in a bad way.
segments.zh: 我认为有一种灵性，这种想法是我们有一个气，我们的身体有积极和消极的力量，有时创伤或大事件会使这种气，嗯，它会以一种坏的方式影响它。

segments.en: So the chi is unbalanced.
segments.zh: 所以气是不平衡的。

segments.en: And so a lot of this is about rebalancing your system.
segments.zh: 因此，其中很多是关于重新平衡您的系统。

segments.en: And if you believe that and you really understand that there are certain forces inside your body, then I'm sure this kind of medicine has a positive effect on you.
segments.zh: 如果你相信这一点，并且你真的明白你的身体里有一些力量，那么我相信这种医学对你有积极的影响。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I believe that it does have its ups and downs.
segments.zh: 我相信它确实有起有落。

segments.en: I was very skeptical about it until once, actually, I had a very, very bad headache and somebody took and pushed a pressure point on my finger, on my thumb for about maybe one or two minutes and the headache was gone.
segments.zh: 我对此非常怀疑，直到有一次，我头痛得非常非常严重，有人在我手指上、我拇指上按了一个穴位，大概一两分钟，头痛就消失了。

segments.en: So I was very much amazed.
segments.zh: 所以我非常惊讶。

segments.en: But at the same time, when people are treated maybe for, you know, maybe they can conceive a baby and they're doing these rituals or giving them ginger or different roots to drink and eat and stuff.
segments.zh: 但与此同时，当人们接受治疗时，比如也许他们想怀上孩子，他们会做各种仪式，或者给他们生姜或各种根茎来泡水喝、食用之类的。

segments.en: I don't know if that really does help or what evidence there is that it actually does work.
segments.zh: 我不知道这是否真的有帮助，或者有什么证据表明它确实有效。

segments.en: Well, I think that's something that also is important to look at on an individual basis.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为这一点也需要因人而异地看待。

segments.en: I don't think even some Western medicines help all the time if you're not in a place where you believe that it will work.
segments.zh: 我认为如果你不在一个你相信它会起作用的地方，即使是一些西方药物也不会一直有帮助。

segments.en: But the interesting aspect of it is, of course, so many years ago, we're talking about hundreds or thousands of years ago, when there was no Western medicine and then people were being cured and treated by these techniques, which actually worked.
segments.zh: 但有趣的一点是，当然，很多很多年前，我们说的是几百甚至几千年前，那时还没有西医，人们却靠这些技术被治愈、被治疗，而这些技术确实有效。

segments.en: So there is a very interesting aspect that maybe even Western medicine can learn from traditional medicine like this.
segments.zh: 所以有一个非常有趣的方面，甚至西医也可以从这样的传统医学中学习。

segments.en: Definitely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: So it's an interesting topic, Oriental medicine, Western medicine, but we want to know what you think about it.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的话题，东方医学，西医，但我们想知道你对此有何看法。

segments.en: We also want to know in your home country, do you have a traditional kind of medicine or any medical alternatives to Western medicine?
segments.zh: 我们还想知道，在您的祖国，您是否有传统医学，或者西医之外的替代疗法？

segments.en: Let us know, our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 让我们知道，我们的网站是 Englishpod.com。

segments.en: All right, we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好，到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
